facts.statement: Simosaurus fossils found in France and Germany date back approximately 230 million years to the Middle Triassic period.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in deposits in France and Germany that are roughly 230 million years old.

facts.statement: Simosaurus reached a length of between 3 and 4 meters.
facts.quote: Simosaurus grew from 3 to 4 m in length.

facts.statement: Simosaurus possessed a blunt, flattened head featuring large upper temporal fossae located behind the eyes.
facts.quote: It has a blunt, flattened head and large openings behind its eyes called upper temporal fossae.

facts.statement: Unlike other nothosaurs, Simosaurus had blunt teeth likely adapted for crushing hard-shelled prey.
facts.quote: Simosaurus also differs from other nothosaurs in that it has blunt teeth that were probably used for crushing hard-shelled organisms.

facts.statement: Simosaurus had a jaw joint positioned far back, extending beyond the main part of the skull.
facts.quote: The jaw joint is set far back, projecting beyond the main portion of the skull.

facts.statement: The type species Simosaurus gaillardoti was named in 1842 by the German paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer.
facts.quote: The type species of Simosaurus, S. gaillardoti, was named by German paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1842.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Simosaurus were discovered in Lunéville, France.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Simosaurus, those described by von Meyer, were found in Lunéville, France.

facts.statement: A complete skull of Simosaurus was discovered by Duke William of Württemberg and sent to von Meyer in 1842.
facts.quote: Duke William of Württemberg discovered a complete skull and sent it to von Meyer in 1842.

facts.statement: Simosaurus had a dorsoventrally flattened trunk and well-developed vertebrae that restricted side-to-side swimming movements.
facts.quote: Simosaurus has well-developed vertebrae and a dorsoventrally flattened trunk that would have inhibited side-to-side movement.

facts.statement: Simosaurus likely generated most of its swimming thrust through a powerful downstroke of its forelimbs, indicated by well-developed humeral crests and a large pectoral girdle.
facts.quote: The humerus has well-developed crests and the underside of the pectoral girdle is large, suggesting that the forelimbs had a powerful downstroke and provided most of the thrust required for swimming.

facts.statement: Simosaurus was likely a moderately powerful swimmer with a locomotion style transitional between early sauropterygian undulation and plesiosaur flipper-driven swimming.
facts.quote: Simosaurus was probably a moderately powerful swimmer with a locomotion that was transitional between the lateral undulation of early sauropterygians and the strong flipper-driven swimming of plesiosaurs.

facts.statement: Simosaurus is often considered a durophagous reptile that fed on organisms with hard shells due to its blunt teeth.
facts.quote: Because it has blunt teeth, Simosaurus is often thought to have been durophagous, meaning that it ate organisms with hard shells.

facts.statement: Simosaurus possessed a long jaw structure resembling that of reptiles capable of snapping bites.
facts.quote: The long jaw of Simosaurus more closely resembles those of reptiles that have snapping bites.

facts.statement: Simosaurus likely fed on moderately hard-shelled organisms including Ceratites ammonites and holostean fish.
facts.quote: It probably fed on moderately hard-shelled organisms such as Ceratites and holostean fish.

facts.statement: Simosaurus uniquely combined muscles for rapid jaw snapping with muscles providing crushing power at the rear of the jaw.
facts.quote: The combination of muscles that quickly snap the jaw shut and muscles that provide crushing power at the back of the jaw is unique to Simosaurus.

facts.statement: Simosaurus belongs to the family Simosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Simosauridae

facts.statement: Simosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Simosaurus fossils found in France originate from the upper Muschelkalk formation of the Ladinian stage in the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: These were found in the upper Muschelkalk, which dates back to the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: Simosaurus first appears in the nodosus biozone, characterized by abundant fossils of the ammonite Ceratites nodosus.
facts.quote: Simosaurus first appears in the nodosus biozone, where fossils of the ammonite Ceratites nodosus are abundant.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding the classification of Simosaurus, with some researchers considering it a pachypleurosaur or a primitive sauropterygian rather than a nothosaur.
facts.quote: It is usually classified as a nothosaur, but has also been considered a pachypleurosaur or a more primitive sauropterygian.
